craft_notes: Sthāyin: inward close — made-of-That as the āhnika's seal. Sanskrit-first: ābhyantaram yathā (inward-thus) kept; dhāraṇayā kept holding (not seeing/worshipping); tatra tatra kept here-there doubled; tanmayībhāvaḥ kept the identity noun — the last word of the chapter is identity. Rows: 9 (here/there doubling), 1 (‘being made of That’ closes — tanmayībhāva end-weight, the seal), 12 (whole-unit śānta-fall into identity). Close: 'the state of being made of That.' Rejected: adding a valediction — killed: identity IS the close; 'circles of earth' reordering — killed: pārthivādau keeps earthen-and-rest. Read aloud: IN-ward, THUS: BY-HOLD-ing-EARTH-and-OTH-er-FORMED-forms — HERE, THERE, IN-the-EARTH-en AND-OTH-er-CIR-cles — THE-state OF-be-ing-MADE-of-THAT.

lines: Inward, thus: by holding earth-and-other-formed forms —
here, there, in the earthen and other circles —
the state of being made of That.
l4.sanskrit_cite: ābhyantaraṃ yathā tattaddharādirūpadhāraṇayā tatra tatra pārthivādau cakre tanmayībhāvaḥ

reads_against.argmap: What is the inward bath? → The ābhyantara bath is dhāraṇā of the same forms in pārthiva-cakra circles — the identity clause (tanmayībhāvaḥ) closes the āhnika.
c1_essence: The inward bath holds earth-and-other forms in earthen circles — being-made-of-That.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vidhi weight (quiescence carrying ritual order)
